rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes liquid-metal dealloying in molten Cu to selectively remove Ti-rich channels from a Ti-doped W–Cu precursor, whereas the paper used LMD on a WTaVTi RHEA precursor to replace Ti-rich interdendritic regions with Cu. Both involve the same kind of intervention (LMD in molten Cu) and the same lever (selective removal of Ti-rich regions), but the precursor material system differs (Ti-doped W–Cu vs. WTaVTi RHEA).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions high-temperature dealloying with molten Cu but does not specify temperature, time, or atmosphere. The paper used 1200 °C for 96 h in vacuum-sealed silica. Both share the same broad regime (high-temperature LMD in molten Cu), but the hypothesis lacks the paper's specific conditions.
